summary: Steady-state throughput cliff in dedicated pool correlated with many tenants pinning large-models causing NVLink fanout saturation
description:
Issue summary: During the customer’s dedicated capacity window we observed a multi-hour p50/p99 throughput cliff (20-40% reduction) without corresponding CPU/GPU memory pressure signals. Impact: customer requests saw elevated queueing and retry behavior, causing downstream timeouts. Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated-wo-34), region us-west-2, customers pinned several large models to fixed versions.

Observed behavior: Throughput drops occur at steady state after ~30–90 minutes of mixed short and long streams. GPU utilization remained high but NVLink utilization spiked and stayed near saturation. Batches were smaller and serialization increased. No driver crashes or GPU OOMs recorded.

Expected behavior: Stable throughput with occasional transient variance during autoscale events. NVLink utilization should remain below saturation for the pool mix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated pool with 8x A100-40GB (nvlink enabled) and default scheduler settings.
2) From multiple tenants (10+), pin large transformer variants (llama2-13b-q4 and redwood-compat-7b) to immutable versions and direct traffic at steady QPS (mixed short/long streams).
3) Maintain a sustained mix: 70% short request streams (<=128 tokens) and 30% long streaming requests (>=1k tokens) for 60+ minutes.
4) Observe throughput and NVLink metrics on the serving nodes and pool aggregator dashboards for 2 hours.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:27:42Z scheduler: placement-delay median +1.8s correlating with NVLink queue depth
2026-03-10T15:30:00Z customer-requests: increased retry count +18% and p99 latency +45%
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support found no GPU driver faults or OOMs on the nodes serving DocuFlow.
Telemetry shows persistent high NVLink transmit rates coincident with throughput cliffs; PCIe metrics normal.
Autoscaler did not trigger scale-out because overall GPU occupancy remained within configured thresholds; however effective batch packing fell sharply.
We correlated tenant model pinning + interleaved long-streams as the common factor across affected nodes.
Scheduler logs show increased serialization at the inter-node transfer stage when model-shard fanout exceeded 6 peers.
Noisy-tenant detection heuristics did not flag the tenants because each individual QPS stayed below per-tenant thresholds; aggregate behavior produced fabric saturation.
hypothesis: Many tenants pinning large model variants caused simultaneous KV-cache warming + frequent cross-GPU KV fetches which increased NVLink fanout and saturated the fabric.
Saturated NVLink increased per-batch latency, which reduced effective batching window and led to steady-state throughput cliffs without changing per-GPU utilization metrics.
Autoscaler thresholds (based on GPU util and queue length) are insufficiently sensitive to NVLink fabric saturation; autoscaler therefore failed to scale proactively.
No single tenant breached noisy-neighbor QPS thresholds so existing isolation heuristics did not preemptively throttle or bin tenants.
mitigation_attempts: 1) Temporarily moved DocuFlow traffic to a different dedicated pool with fewer pinned model variants to observe recovery (partial throughput restoration after 25m).
2) Applied a short-term scheduler tweak to prefer colocated placement for pinned-model tenants (reduced cross-node KV fetches by ~30%).
3) Enabled conservative autoscale override to force-add two nodes; this restored batch packing but added cost and required careful rollback plan.
4) Notified customer about recommended prompt shaping to reduce long continuous streams until we ship a permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround applied: migrated the customer off the saturated pool for immediate relief and enabled a temporary autoscale override. Engineering action items opened to add NVLink/PCIe fabric saturation as a first-class autoscaler input and to implement an aggregate-model-pinning detector that treats many small tenants pinning the same large models as a potential noisy-neighbor. Planned rollout: autoscaler input change and scheduler heuristic landed behind feature flag in serving-runtime PR #2891; targeted canary on lower-traffic pools next week. Postmortem scheduled with SRE and product to update docs and customer guidance.
